ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Monitoring a synthesis inhibitor

A 38-year-old patient is being considered for zileuton. Baseline tests show active liver disease with substantially elevated aminotransferases. Which organ-specific toxicity is most relevant when deciding whether this medication is appropriate?

  1. Hepatotoxicity
  2. Retinal pigment deposition
  3. Irreversible ototoxicity
  4. Hemorrhagic cystitis
  5. Gingival hyperplasia
Answer and explanation

Hepatotoxicity

Zileuton can cause liver injury and requires attention to baseline and follow-up liver tests.

Option explanations

Hepatotoxicity: Zileuton can cause liver injury and requires attention to baseline and follow-up liver tests.

Retinal pigment deposition: This is not the characteristic monitoring issue for zileuton.

Irreversible ototoxicity: This is more characteristic of drugs such as aminoglycosides.

Hemorrhagic cystitis: This is associated with certain chemotherapy agents rather than zileuton.

Gingival hyperplasia: This is classically associated with phenytoin.
